cues.en: Instructor: In the previous video, I told you about cross validation and I mentioned that one of the main purposes of cross validation is to compute classification accuracy.
cues.zh: 講師：前一部影片介紹交叉驗證，提到主要用途之一是計算分類準確率。

cues.en: And so what I want to do in this video is talk about how classification accuracy works.
cues.zh: 這部影片要談分類準確率如何運作。

cues.en: So how models classify data.
cues.zh: 模型如何分類資料。

cues.en: And I'm also going to discuss the differences between model testing and hypothesis testing for statistical significance
cues.zh: 也會討論模型檢驗和假設檢定的差異，一邊用 P 值評估統計顯著性，

cues.en: with P-values and hypothesis testing with regards to classification accuracy.
cues.zh: 另一邊則從分類準確率的角度檢驗假設。

cues.en: And basically you'll see that these are complimentary approaches.
cues.zh: 基本上，會看到兩者互補。

cues.en: They tell different things about the data and they are both useful.
cues.zh: 它們透露資料的不同資訊，而且都很有用。

cues.en: It's not like you have to pick either one of these two.
cues.zh: 不需要二選一。

cues.en: Okay, so let's begin with a description of how classification works, how models can classify data.
cues.zh: 先說明分類如何運作，模型如何分類資料。

cues.en: So let's start with an example.
cues.zh: 從例子開始。

cues.en: So let's say we want to predict whether a student is going to pass or fail her statistics course, and we say that the main predictors in the model
cues.zh: 假設想預測某位學生是否通過統計課，模型主要預測變數，

cues.en: is going to be study hours, number of alcoholic drinks consumed, let's say per week and web surfing hours.
cues.zh: 是讀書時數、例如每週喝幾杯酒，以及上網時數。

cues.en: And these three variables we use to predict the outcome.
cues.zh: 用這三個變數預測結果。

cues.en: So to be clear, we have three independent variables here.
cues.zh: 說清楚，有三個自變數。

cues.en: How many hours does she spend studying?
cues.zh: 花幾小時讀書？

cues.en: How many drinks she has, let's say per week?
cues.zh: 例如每週喝幾杯酒？

cues.en: And how many hours, let's say per day she spends wasting time on the internet?
cues.zh: 例如每天花幾小時在網路上浪費時間？

cues.en: So, and then the outcome measure is binary.
cues.zh: 結果量值則是二元的。

cues.en: So the dependent measure is binary here, it's either pass or fail.
cues.zh: 依變數是二元，只可能及格或不及格。

cues.en: Okay, so this is an example of a logistic regression.
cues.zh: 這是邏輯斯迴歸的例子。

cues.en: The analysis approach you would use here is called a logistic regression.
cues.zh: 使用的分析方法稱為邏輯斯迴歸。

cues.en: Now, if that term sounds fancy and mysterious and ether real, then of course it should, I haven't yet talked about logistic regression.
cues.zh: 如果這個詞聽起來高深、神祕、飄渺，當然應該如此，因為還沒介紹。

cues.en: You'll learn more about it later.
cues.zh: 後面會學更多。

cues.en: The details are not important for now.
cues.zh: 目前細節不重要。

cues.en: For now, you can just know that we have three independent variables and that's used to predict a binary outcome.
cues.zh: 只要知道有三個自變數，用來預測二元結果。

cues.en: Okay, so the model has these three predictors.
cues.zh: 所以模型有三個預測變數。

cues.en: So we input the study hours, the drinking and the web surfing into the model, and the model gives an output.
cues.zh: 將讀書時數、飲酒與上網資料輸入模型，模型產生輸出。

cues.en: Now the thing is, which you'll also learn later in the section on regression, the model doesn't actually output a label.
cues.zh: 之後迴歸那一章會學到，模型其實不直接輸出標籤。

cues.en: It outputs a probability of a given label.
cues.zh: 而是某個標籤的機率。

cues.en: So let's say, you know, we're gonna call, pass has a value of zero and fail has a value of one.
cues.zh: 假設把及格定為 0，不及格定為 1。

cues.en: So the model will tell us based on this particular student's behavior that this student has a 23% chance of passing and of course a 77% chance of failing.
cues.zh: 根據這位學生的行為，模型說她有 23% 機會及格，當然也有 77% 機會不及格。

cues.en: Now, obviously these are complimentary.
cues.zh: 顯然，兩者互補。

cues.en: The probability theory tells us that the sum of all possible probabilities has to add up to 100%.
cues.zh: 機率理論告訴我們，所有可能結果的機率總和必須為 100%。

cues.en: So, either you pass or fail the exam, there's nothing else, there's no other options, okay?
cues.zh: 不是及格就是不及格，沒有其他選項，好嗎？

cues.en: So then what we do is we threshold the model output.
cues.zh: 接著對模型輸出設門檻。

cues.en: In this case because we have a binary output, it's appropriate to threshold at 50%.
cues.zh: 因為是二元輸出，這裡用 50% 門檻合適。

cues.en: And then this is called classification.
cues.zh: 這稱為分類。

cues.en: So then the model actually outputs 77% chance of failing.
cues.zh: 模型實際輸出不及格機率 77%。

cues.en: And then we say because 77 is higher than 50, we predict the model predicts that this student is going to fail her stats exam.
cues.zh: 因為 77 大於 50，所以預測，模型預測，這位學生統計考試不及格。

cues.en: Its a pity but, you know, that happens.
cues.zh: 很可惜，但確實會發生。

cues.en: Okay, and this is how classification works.
cues.zh: 這就是分類的運作方式。

cues.en: Okay, so classification is mainly appropriate for categorical data like nominal and ordinal data.
cues.zh: 分類主要適合名目、次序等類別資料。

cues.en: It's kind of technically possible to do classification on discrete data, but that's generally not how it's done.
cues.zh: 技術上對離散資料分類也可以，但通常不是這樣做。

cues.en: It's usually done on nominal or ordinal data.
cues.zh: 通常用於名目或次序資料。

cues.en: How about interval or ratio data?
cues.zh: 區間或比率資料呢？

cues.en: Is it possible to classify in interval or ratio data?
cues.zh: 有可能對區間或比率資料分類嗎？

cues.en: Well, obviously the answer is no, otherwise I wouldn't phrase the question like this, but I would like you to think about this.
cues.zh: 顯然答案是不行，不然不會這樣問，但希望你思考。

cues.en: Pause the video if you want some more time to think about it.
cues.zh: 需要更多時間，可以暫停影片。

cues.en: I'm not gonna tell you the answer.
cues.zh: 我不會告訴你答案。

cues.en: I want you to come up with the answer yourself.
cues.zh: 希望你自己想出來。

cues.en: Why is it not possible to classify interval or ratio data?
cues.zh: 為什麼不能對區間或比率資料分類？

cues.en: Alright, so moving on, the model prediction ends up being compared against the reality, and we can come up with a table like this.
cues.zh: 接著將模型預測和真實情況比較，可以得到這樣的表。

cues.en: So we say the model output and then this is the predicted category.
cues.zh: 這是模型輸出，這是預測類別。

cues.en: Here is the reality because of course in the end we're gonna know whether the student actually passed or failed that's gonna tell us whether this is a good model.
cues.zh: 這裡是真實情況，最後當然會知道學生到底及不及格，這能告訴我們模型好不好。

cues.en: So here, the reality matches the prediction.
cues.zh: 這裡真實情況和預測相符。

cues.en: So we have an accuracy, we'll call this accuracy one, and here and here and here the model predicted that the student would fail the exam, but she actually passed the exam.
cues.zh: 所以準確，記為 1；這裡、這裡和這裡，模型預測學生不及格，但她實際及格。

cues.en: So this is a discrepancy, the model was inaccurate here.
cues.zh: 這有差異，模型在這裡不準確。

cues.en: So, now computing the model accuracy is actually really simple.
cues.zh: 計算模型準確率其實很簡單。

cues.en: We just average over these four values.
cues.zh: 把這四個值平均。

cues.en: So in this particular case, the model accuracy is 75%.
cues.zh: 這個情況，準確率為 75%。

cues.en: Now needless to say, you know, hopefully in real data you're gonna have more than four data points like this, but, you know, this is just a simple example.
cues.zh: 不用說，希望真實資料不只四個點，但只是簡單例子。

cues.en: So how does cross validation fit into all this?
cues.zh: 交叉驗證如何融入？

cues.en: I haven't yet talked about cross validation.
cues.zh: 我還沒談交叉驗證。

cues.en: So the idea of classification and cross validation is that you construct your statistical model based on the training set.
cues.zh: 分類和交叉驗證的概念，是根據訓練集建立統計模型。

cues.en: Let's say there's a hundred students in the course.
cues.zh: 假設班上有 100 位學生。

cues.en: So you construct a model based on the data from 90 randomly selected students, and then you test the model on the other 10 students.
cues.zh: 用 90 位隨機選取學生的資料建模，再用其他 10 位測試。

cues.en: So there's 10 students that you haven't exposed to the models, the model has never seen these data before.
cues.zh: 這 10 位的資料，模型從未見過。

cues.en: And then the model will try to predict whether each of these 10 students will pass or fail the exam.
cues.zh: 模型試著預測，每位是否通過考試。

cues.en: Okay, so that's a brief overview of how classification works with cross validation.
cues.zh: 這是分類搭配交叉驗證的簡介。

cues.en: I realize that's a little bit high level, I'm not talking about any details, I haven't shown you any equations or formulas or how to come up with these models that will come later in the section on regression.
cues.zh: 知道這有點概略，沒談細節，也沒有展示方程式、公式或如何建立模型，迴歸章會介紹。

cues.en: For now, I hope you have a general intuitive idea of classification and cross validation because you also now understand how
cues.zh: 目前希望你對分類和交叉驗證有一般直覺，因為也已理解

cues.en: kind of traditional hypothesis testing works with getting P-values and rejecting the null hypothesis or failing to reject it.
cues.zh: 傳統假設檢定如何取得 P 值、拒絕或無法拒絕虛無假設。

cues.en: So, here are some complimentary comparisons between the P-value approach and the classification approach.
cues.zh: 這裡有些 P 值方法和分類方法的互補比較。

cues.en: So with P-values, what you are doing is testing the probability of the sample or of observing the sample statistic or of having a model like this by chance,
cues.zh: P 值是在虛無假設為真時，檢驗樣本、觀察到樣本統計量，或偶然產生這樣模型的機率，

cues.en: given that the null hypothesis is true.
cues.zh: 條件是虛無假設成立。

cues.en: Now with classification accuracy, what you're actually testing is how closely the model output the threshold and binerized model output matches some observed outcome measure.
cues.zh: 分類準確率實際檢驗的，是模型輸出經門檻二元化後，和觀察到的結果量值多吻合。

cues.en: And again, that's generally a categorical measure.
cues.zh: 這通常是類別量值。

cues.en: You can think also of deep learning, which is essentially building classification models.
cues.zh: 也可以想深度學習，基本上就是建立分類模型。

cues.en: So the observed outcome measure is, you know, whether the picture was of a unicorn or a penguin, and then the model is gonna classify the picture as a unicorn or a penguin
cues.zh: 觀察結果是圖片為獨角獸或企鵝，再由模型將圖片分類為獨角獸、企鵝，

cues.en: or one of you know, a hundred other categories.
cues.zh: 或其他上百種類之一。

cues.en: So with P-values, you can actually get a separate P-value for each parameter in the model.
cues.zh: P 值方法可以為模型中每個參數，各自取得 P 值。

cues.en: You learn more about this later in the sections on ANOVA and regression models.
cues.zh: 後面 ANOVA 和迴歸模型章節會多介紹。

cues.en: But basically when you have a model like what the example I gave you here, you can actually say what is the specific contribution of hours spent studying,
cues.zh: 基本上，如果有剛才那種模型，就能分別說出讀書時數、

cues.en: number of alcoholic drinks and number of hours spent wasting time on the web.
cues.zh: 飲酒杯數，以及上網浪費時間時數的特定貢獻。

cues.en: You can get P-values and estimate sizes for each of those models.
cues.zh: 可以取得每個模型的 P 值和估計大小。

cues.en: With classification accuracy, it can be possible to get individual parameter contributions, but it's actually more common with classification accuracy
cues.zh: 分類準確率有時也能取得個別參數貢獻，但更常見的是，

cues.en: to consider the entire model all at once.
cues.zh: 一次考慮整個模型。

cues.en: And as the models get more and more complicated, it becomes more and more difficult to assign credit to any individual parameter in the model.
cues.zh: 模型越複雜，就越難將功勞分配給任一個別參數。

cues.en: Okay, the P-value approach has analytic solutions with well-established mathematical theory.
cues.zh: P 值方法有解析解，以及成熟的數學理論。

cues.en: That means that even without having any actual data, you can, you know, in theory you can go up to a chalkboard with a piece of chalk and maybe you also need an eraser
cues.zh: 表示即使沒有實際資料，理論上也能拿粉筆到黑板，也許還要板擦，

cues.en: and you can prove mathematically using math that these methods are the right solution, that they're the right thing to do.
cues.zh: 用數學證明這些方法是正確的解、正確做法。

cues.en: They give you the good approach, they give you the best possible way to analyze these data.
cues.zh: 提供好的方法、分析資料的最佳可能方式。

cues.en: And with classification accuracy, it's a little bit different.
cues.zh: 分類準確率稍有不同。

cues.en: Classification and cross validation isn't really based on strong old, you know, mathematical theory.
cues.zh: 分類與交叉驗證，不是真正建立在悠久、強大的數學理論上。

cues.en: Instead, it is based on sensible empirical algorithms that people have refined over time.
cues.zh: 而是基於合理的實證演算法，經過時間逐步精煉。

cues.en: And because there's also some measure of stochasticity, there's some randomness that comes in with this classification accuracy approach, the results may actually differ each time you rerun
cues.zh: 因為分類準確率方法有某種隨機性，每次重新執行

cues.en: the model, even if you're using the same data.
cues.zh: 模型，即使資料相同，結果也可能不同。

cues.en: So you can see that's a little bit different.
cues.zh: 可以看到有點不同。

cues.en: Again, I don't mean to suggest that either one of these is better or worse, they're just different.
cues.zh: 再次提醒，並不是說哪個比較好或差，只是不同。

cues.en: The P-value approach of null hypothesis testing is appropriate for pretty much, you know, a really wide range of models with a really wide range of variables.
cues.zh: 以 P 值檢驗虛無假設，適用於很廣泛的模型、變數。

cues.en: It's very versatile approach that is generally applicable.
cues.zh: 用途多元，通常普遍適用。

cues.en: Classification accuracy is used only for certain kinds of models and certain kinds of data types.
cues.zh: 分類準確率則只適用於特定模型、特定資料類型。

cues.en: It's not generally applicable, it's not necessarily the case that, you know, any kind of dataset, any kind of hypothesis is appropriate for classification accuracy.
cues.zh: 不是普遍適用，不是任意資料集、任意假設，都適合分類準確率。

cues.en: The P-value methods can be sensitive to extreme ends.
cues.zh: P 值方法可能對極端 N 很敏感。

cues.en: So this is extremely small ends or extremely large ends.
cues.zh: 也就是極小或極大的樣本數 N。

cues.en: And you'll see why over the next several sections in T-test, and correlation, ANOVA and regression, because you'll see that the computation
cues.zh: 接下來 t 檢定、相關、ANOVA 和迴歸章，會看到原因，因為計算

cues.en: of the P-value is dependent in part on the number of samples you have in your dataset.
cues.zh: P 值，部分取決於資料集有多少樣本。

cues.en: And classification accuracy approaches tend to be more robust to sample sizes.
cues.zh: 分類準確率方法通常對樣本大小更穩健。

cues.en: Certainly also on the large side of things, and I mentioned this in the very beginning of the lecture, but I wanna stress this now at the end because this is pretty important.
cues.zh: 尤其在樣本很多時。一開始提過，但結尾想再強調，因為很重要。

cues.en: It's not a competition, it's not like, you know, it's P value versus classification accuracy and you gotta stick to one camp or the other.
cues.zh: 這不是競爭，不是 P 值對分類準確率，必須選一個陣營。

cues.en: These are just different approaches.
cues.zh: 只是不同方法。

cues.en: Sometimes the P-value null hypothesis testing approach is more sensible.
cues.zh: 有時 P 值虛無假設檢定比較合理。

cues.en: Sometimes classification accuracy is more sensible.
cues.zh: 有時分類準確率比較合理。

cues.en: Certainly you can use both approaches when appropriate and they're not going to like conflict or interfere with each other.
cues.zh: 適當時當然可以兩者都用，不會衝突或互相干擾。

cues.en: Okay, so in this lecture I gave you an overview of how model classification works in combination with the cross validation approach
cues.zh: 這堂課概述模型分類如何結合交叉驗證，

cues.en: and how that relates to statistical significance, that kind of traditional null hypothesis P value approach of evaluating models.
cues.zh: 以及和統計顯著性，也就是傳統以虛無假設 P 值評估模型的方法，有什麼關係。
